title: What If All Clothes Disappeared Overnight?
description:
What if you woke up and every piece of clothing on Earth had disappeared overnight, and it was permanent?

In this 2D animated What-If story, you live through the strangest three days of your life: the panic, the breaking news, the awkward walk down the street, a very confusing trip to the park, and one unforgettable visit to Mia's apartment. And then you find out what actually changes when everyone is in the same situation.

This is a family-friendly cartoon. Everything is censored and kept light, funny and heartwarming.

title: What If You Were Stuck in a Car With Your Crush?
description:
What if a blizzard trapped you in a car with the person you've liked for two years… and your phone held a "grocery list" that is very much not a grocery list?

Three days. One car. One blanket that smells like your dog. And half a jar of Grandma's pickles.

Real science in this story:
• Carbon monoxide: why a buried tailpipe is deadly, and why rescuers say to clear it every hour
• Arthur Aron's 36 Questions (1997): how strangers become close in 45 minutes
• The Capilano Suspension Bridge study (Vancouver, 1974): why fear can feel like a crush

If you were stuck with your crush, what's the first thing you'd say? Tell us in the comments.

title: What If Your CRUSH Could Feel Everything You Do?!
What If You Could See Who Loves You?
tags: what if you could see who loves you
how to tell if someone likes you
how to tell if a girl likes you
who has a crush on you
description:
▶ NEW VIDEO: What If You Were the Only Man on an Island of 100 Amazons? https://youtu.be/UtXsABU4Cek

What if you could see who loves you? This what if animation gives you three days of hearts above everyone's head: who hates you, who doesn't care, and who loves you 100%.

Imagine you wake up tomorrow, and there's a heart above everyone's head. Black means they don't like you. Gray means you don't matter to them. Red means they like you. And 100% means they're in love with you.

But there's a catch: day one, you only see black hearts. Day two, gray. Day three, red. Then they vanish for a whole year. Your best friend turns out to be at −100%. And the person who loves you 100% is the last person you'd ever guess.

Along the way, the real science of how to tell if someone likes you: a real smile versus a polite one, pupils that widen, and why believing someone likes you can make it come true.

So... whose heart would you check first? Tell us in the comments.

Real facts in this video
• A real smile usually also tightens the muscles around the eyes (the "Duchenne smile"), a polite one often only moves the mouth: Ekman, Davidson & Friesen, Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 58(2), 1990. https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.58.2.342
• Social circles come in layers of about 5, about 15 and about 150 people: Zhou, Sornette, Hill & Dunbar, Proceedings of the Royal Society B 272(1561), 2005. https://doi.org/10.1098/rspb.2004.2970
• People who were led to believe a partner liked them behaved more warmly, and the partner came to like them more: Curtis & Miller, Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 51(2), 1986. https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.51.2.284
• Mutual gaze between dogs and their owners raised oxytocin in both: Nagasawa et al., Science 348(6232), 2015. https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1261022
• About two thirds of cats tested (64% of kittens) were securely attached to their owners, close to the share seen in human infants: Vitale, Behnke & Udell, Current Biology 29(18), 2019. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cub.2019.08.036
• Pupils tend to widen when we look at something or someone we find interesting or pleasant: Hess, Scientific American 212(4), 1965. https://doi.org/10.1038/scientificamerican0465-46

Everyone in this video is fictional.

title: What If You Could See Everyone's Body Count?
description:
Every grown-up in this city has a number above their head: how many people they've slept with. Only you can see them.
Yours is zero. Your mom's is one. Your dad's is forty-seven. And before this is over, one person will say their real number to your face.

Would you have told him? Tell me in the comments.

title: What If Your CRUSH Was Tokyo's DRIFT QUEEN?
description:
What if you got lost on your first day in Tokyo… and ended up becoming the city's newest drift champion? 🏁

You were 18, knew exactly three Japanese phrases, and took the wrong train. That's how you met Mei, a famous drift racer with grease on her face and zero patience for useless tourists. But when a crash takes her off the track just 14 weeks before the Midnight Cup, the biggest drift tournament of the year, her team needs a driver… and somehow, it's you.

Stalled engines, spun-out qualifiers, a rival named Kaito who thinks you're a joke, and a girl who keeps saying she's "mostly kidding." Can the lost tourist really become a drift monster?

description:

title: What IF You Could See Who Will Become Famous?
description:
What if you could see who will become famous? 🌟 You glance at a stranger, and a glowing symbol appears above their head. Right now, nobody knows their name—but one day, millions will. Then you spot the same symbol above someone sitting beside you in class. What would you do with a glimpse of their future?

In this animated what-if scenario, we imagine life with the power to recognise tomorrow’s biggest stars: hearing a future chart-topper sing to an empty room, watching an unknown athlete practise, and discovering that your quietest friend might someday be recognised everywhere. But knowing someone will become famous wouldn’t tell you when—or why.

Would you encourage their ambitions, keep your visions secret, or try to become part of their journey? Telling someone they’re destined for fame could change their decisions before they ever get there. And what happens when a symbol appears above someone who seems determined to stay out of the spotlight?

This future-seeing adventure explores ambition, friendship, and the unexpected consequences of knowing who the world will notice next. Would you help people find their moment—or become so focused on their future that you overlooked who they are today?
